entries.change: Replaced links that had become unsafe with archived copies of the original pages: the Linguistics Network phonology tutorial (the domain now redirects to gambling sites) and four Speech Recognition Virtual Kitchen pages (the domain lapsed; the previous archived copies showed a for-sale or parked page); the site will no longer link to either domain. Retired Smithsonian Speech Synthesis History Project pages now open 2016 archived copies; one link labelled 'Holmes' on the original page opens Mattingly's 1974 review, and its label now says so.

Original catalog checked entry by entry against the archived ISCA pages: restored original wording where the 31 August transcription had shortened or reworded entries (for example the wav2vec, sequence-modelling, formant-synthesis and concatenative-synthesis entries, and the Stanford lecture dates), removed details that were not on the original pages, and added two items the transcription had missed: Andreas Spanias's 1994 speech coding tutorial review and the HTK homepage link. The original catalog now has 105 entries.

Link repairs made in the 31 August rebuild, now listed here: Roger Moore's Lecture 5 slides and audio use the staffwww.dcs.shef.ac.uk mirror of the same files; two speech.zone links follow the course's renamed synthesis module; the 2021 ISCA Medal lecture links to its ISCA Archive page; a Google search link was replaced by the direct YouTube link to the same video; a broken LDC anchor points to www.ldc.upenn.edu. Today: Yao Wang's speech coding notes use the new NYU address of the same PDF, five http links (the USC real-time MRI page, the wav2vec 2.0 guide and three Kaldi documentation pages) now use https; and the original page's malformed link to the Interspeech 2022 tutorial's review paper now opens it on arXiv.

Updated 50 extension entries after checking each against its own page: current versions (Praat 7.0.02, ESPnet 202610, SpeechBrain 1.1.1, whisper.cpp 1.9.4, sherpa-onnx 1.13.8, Piper 1.8.0, Montreal Forced Aligner 3.4.2, librosa 1.0.0, NeMo Speech 3.0); moved repositories and courses (CosyVoice, SEP-28k, CMU 11-751 Fall 2026, CMU 11-785, the HSE course's complete 2025 branch); corrected access and cost notes (GigaSpeech, Multilingual LibriSpeech, the EPFL DSP specialization); past events written in the past tense with next editions (Interspeech, Speech Prosody, JSALT, VoicePrivacy, SPSC, CHiME, URGENT); the Blizzard Challenge now links to its current official site.

Links now checked every day, with archived copies shown for links that fail three days in a row; the UCLA Phonetics Lab Archive (expired security certificate) and the HTK homepage (server errors) show archived copies for now. Email and GitHub issues are now read three times a day. The 'How this site is maintained' and 'Suggest a resource or correction' sections describe the process. The notice at the top of the page again carries the full disclosure. Search fixes: section labels stay visible while filtering, results appear right below the search box, and searches for SIGs or seminars point to the ISCA SIG Atlas.

Replaced the embedded SIG directory and event lists with a direct link to the independent ISCA SIG Atlas. Added topic shortcuts, source filters, shareable multi-word search and a clear empty state; improved keyboard and mobile navigation. All 104 original entries and 118 extensions are preserved. Resource content and link-audit dates are unchanged.

Disclaimer strengthened across the site at the owner's request: SCOOT 2.0 is not an official ISCA publication, nothing on it has been verified by any human, and the whole site is the output of Hung-yi Lee casually prompting an AI agent (Claude Fable 5) to see what AI agents can currently do. Banner, About, SIG-part disclosure and the masthead line all updated to say so plainly.

Anchored the Spoken LLM Benchmark Atlas under SCOOT 2.0: a new Benchmarks section links the daily-updated index of spoken-LLM benchmarks (368 benchmarks / 19 categories / 15,468 sourced result cells at the time of writing), which lives on its own page because of its size and daily rebuild; the atlas page now carries SCOOT 2.0 attribution and links back.

Repaired three original-catalog links to www.synsig.org (Speech Technology → Synthesis): the SIG's historical domain has been hijacked and now serves a gambling site while still answering HTTP 200, so the automated link check could not catch it. Main link now points to the SIG's current home at isca-speech.org/SynSIG; the Software and Educational-materials wiki pages point to April 2024 Internet Archive snapshots of the same pages. Entry text unchanged; repair registered in the coverage audit.

Merged the ISCA SIG activities atlas into this page as the 'ISCA SIGs & online events' part: 20 SIG cards with reviewed activities and video resources, the webinar & lecture series tracker, upcoming events, recorded workshop archives, ISCA-level video resources and board notes. The atlas's former standalone address now redirects here. All SIG links were reviewed 31 August 2026 (see 'The SIG part' in the footer).

Fixed catalog QA issues: lecture-title searches now reveal their parent resource, mobile topic navigation is collapsible, link-check provenance is reported from the actual audit timestamp, and the dead Odette Scharenborg Winter School URL was replaced with the author's maintained teaching page containing the same Day 1–5 slides.
Site name confirmed as SCOOT 2.0 (this rebuild supersedes the July 2026 SCOOT 2.0 prototype at the same address).

Site rebuilt around the ORIGINAL ISCA SCOOT topic tree (Overviews / Sound / Signal Processing / Linguistics / Phonetics / Speech Technology / Toolkits / Databases). All 104 resource entries from the original SCOOT pages (26 pages, snapshot 2026-08-31) transcribed and preserved; the 2.0 curated catalog (118 entries) re-mapped as clearly-marked extensions under the original topics, plus three extension topics (Paralinguistics, Clinical & Accessibility, Community). Every link on the page re-verified; dead original links carry Internet Archive snapshot links. Daily-feed tab removed (auto-update paused 2026-08-28).
SCOOT 2.0 prototype launched: curated catalog seeded (all entries link-verified), daily auto-update pipeline for arXiv papers and trending models, community suggestion loop defined.
Deployed publicly on GitHub Pages. Catalog at launch: 122 entries across 10 areas (two Chinese-language course entries deferred — English-language resources prioritized at launch).
